items.prompt: Edges 0--1 weight 10,0--2 weight 1,2--1 weight 1 are given. Why can ordinary unit-edge BFS give the wrong weighted result for node 1?

options.text: Two links cost 2, less than the direct link's 10.
options.why: Fewest links and smallest total latency are different objectives.

options.text: BFS cannot traverse an undirected edge.
options.why: BFS can traverse undirected graphs; ignoring unequal weights is the problem.

options.text: The graph has no route from 0 to 1.
options.why: Both the direct and two-edge routes exist.

options.text: Dijkstra always uses the fewest edges regardless of weight.
options.why: Dijkstra minimizes total nonnegative weight, not hop count alone.

items.explanation: Fewest links and smallest total latency are different objectives.
